title: Chinese startup DexForce trains humanoid robots using virtual data to slash costs
key_facts: Reuters reported on 15 Oct 2026 from Shenzhen that DexForce, a Chinese start-up, trains humanoid robots on synthetic data generated in virtual environments.
The aim is to cut costs and improve training efficiency compared with collecting large volumes of data from human workers repeating tasks in the real world.
Chief executive Jia Kui told Reuters the approach could power a breakthrough akin to the one ChatGPT triggered after 2022.
Jia said reaching 'physical artificial general intelligence' purely through real-world data would need 10 trillion samples.
A screen at the offices shows a virtual robot repeating a task as arm angle, table colour and objects change.
quote_evidence: DexForce is relying on synthetic data generated in virtual environments to cut costs and improve training efficiency.
Trying to achieve 'physical artificial general intelligence' purely through real-world data collection would require 10 trillion samples

China has developed humanoids capable of outperforming humans in running and jumping but the harder commercial test lies in whether they can reliably carry out useful work in factories, offices and the home.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper robot training could speed up useful humanoids, but this is one company's bet.
notes: Reuters original returns 401; read the Reuters text as carried by Oman Observer (opening part only, article appears cut short). Claims are the CEO's.
